skill.name: database-migrations-sql-migrations
skill.description: Plan SQL database migrations with zero-downtime strategies, validation checks, rollback procedures, and performance guidance for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server.
skill.summary: Create safer SQL migration plans with validation, rollback, and zero-downtime strategies.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill contains documentation and code samples; none automatically execute commands or access SQLite files, so all 33 static alerts are false positives for those patterns. However, the rollback and Python examples interpolate unvalidated values into SQL and paths, creating adoption-time injection and file-selection risks. No prompt injection, network access, credential exfiltration, or hidden execution was found.

remediation.issue: The rollback example inserts a positional argument into SQL and filenames without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist migration versions, quote database arguments, constrain generated paths, and bind the version through psql variables instead of SQL string interpolation.

remediation.issue: Python examples insert input-derived table and column names into SQL strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use driver identifier-composition APIs, allowlist schema identifiers, and accept raw query fragments only from trusted application constants.

content.value_statement: Database migrations can lock tables, corrupt data, or leave applications incompatible. This skill creates staged plans with validation, rollback, batching, and zero-downtime strategies.
actual_capabilities: Designs expand-contract and blue-green schema migration plans.
Generates version-controlled SQL migration and rollback outlines.
Provides Flyway and Alembic migration patterns.
Defines pre-migration and post-migration integrity checks.
Plans batched and parallel processing for large tables.
Suggests index management and deployment sequencing to reduce disruption.
limitations: Generated scripts are not executed or tested against your database.
Examples favor PostgreSQL and require adaptation for MySQL or SQL Server.
Accurate plans require schema, engine version, data volume, traffic, and deployment constraints.
Destructive changes still require backups, staging tests, and expert review.

use_cases.title: Add Fields Without Downtime
use_cases.description: Plan a backward-compatible schema change while old and new application versions run together.

use_cases.title: Backfill Large Production Tables
use_cases.description: Define batches, throttling, checkpoints, and validation for a high-volume data migration.

use_cases.title: Build Migration Release Gates
use_cases.description: Create deployment sequencing, rollback criteria, and verification steps for automated delivery workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Column Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe migration plan to add [column] to [table] on [database]. Include prerequisites, validation checks, and rollback steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused, backward-compatible schema addition.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Expand-Contract Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an expand-contract migration for [schema change] while [old version] and [new version] run concurrently. Include deployment order and compatibility checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several application versions share one database.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Large-Table Backfill
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a zero-downtime backfill for [table] containing [row count] rows. Define batch sizing, throttling, progress checks, failure recovery, and index handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for high-volume production data with strict availability targets.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed migration: [plan]. Identify locking, integrity, injection, rollback, and compatibility risks. Produce a revised sequence with go or no-go gates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before approving a complex or destructive production change.

output_examples.input: Add a nullable verified_at column to a busy users table without stopping writes.
output: Expand: add the nullable column without changing existing reads or writes.
Migrate: backfill rows in monitored batches with replica-lag and lock thresholds.
Contract: enforce final constraints only after all application versions use the new column.
Rollback: stop the backfill and revert application behavior before removing schema changes.

output_examples.input: Move order data into a new schema while keeping both application versions available.
output: Create the destination schema and verify constraints before enabling synchronization.
Dual-write new changes, backfill historical rows, and compare counts and checksums.
Switch reads gradually after validation, then retire synchronization during a later release.

output_examples.input: Review a migration that adds a required column to a large production table.
output_examples.output: The direct change may lock the table and reject existing rows. Add the column as nullable, backfill it, validate data, then enforce the constraint.

best_practices: Collect engine version, table size, traffic patterns, replication limits, and recovery objectives before designing the migration.
Separate schema expansion, data backfill, application rollout, and schema contraction into independently verifiable releases.
Test forward and rollback paths with production-like data, then monitor locks, errors, lag, and migration progress.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated migration examples directly in production without environment-specific review and testing.
Do not combine destructive schema changes with application dependencies in one irreversible deployment.
Do not interpolate untrusted table names, column names, versions, or paths into SQL and shell commands.

faq.question: Which database engines does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It targets PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server, although detailed examples favor PostgreSQL.

faq.question: Does the skill execute migrations?
faq.answer: No. It produces plans, scripts, checks, and rollback guidance for you to review and run.

faq.question: Can it guarantee zero downtime?
faq.answer: No. Availability depends on engine behavior, schema size, workload, deployment order, and operational controls.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the current schema, desired change, database version, row counts, traffic profile, deployment process, and recovery objectives.

faq.question: Does it support migration frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes Flyway and Alembic patterns that require adaptation to your project.

faq.question: How should destructive changes be handled?
faq.answer: Use backups, staged compatibility releases, explicit validation gates, tested rollback procedures, and qualified human approval.
